Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD) is a rare progressive genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the SMPD1 gene causing low or absent activity of the enzyme acid sphingomyelinase, resulting in subsequent accumulation of its substrate, sphingomyelin.

Signs and symptoms of excessive lysosomal sphingomyelin storage, such as hepatosplenomegaly and pulmonary impairment, and in a subset of patients, progressive neurological manifestations, have long been recognized as hallmarks of the disease.
